# Adi Midla — Full Portfolio Summary

## Professional introduction

Adi Midla is a third-year B.Tech Computer Science and Engineering student specialising in Gaming Technology at VIT Bhopal University, India. He is developing his abilities through coursework, projects, experimentation, and continuous learning. His central interest is how software and technology can become useful, interactive, and memorable experiences.

## Areas of interest

Programming: C++, Python, Java.  
Computer science: data structures and algorithms, software engineering, and problem solving.  
Interactive development: Unity, game development, XR, and virtual reality.  
Web and emerging technology: web development, AI exploration, and new technologies.

These are current interests and learning areas. The portfolio does not assign proficiency percentages or present every area as professional expertise.

## Project records

### ExamScannerAI

Status: backend prototype; frontend planned.  
The public repository describes a Python/FastAPI backend that accepts exam-paper images, preprocesses them with OpenCV, extracts text with Tesseract OCR, cleans OCR output, detects and separates questions, and returns structured JSON.  
Technologies: Python, FastAPI, OpenCV, Tesseract OCR.  
Repository: https://github.com/adimidla20/ExamScannerAI

### Open Source Audit

Status: coursework.  
A project about Git and open-source software, accompanied by five Bash scripts for system identity, package inspection, disk auditing, log analysis, and manifesto generation.  
Technologies and topics: Bash, Linux, Git, technical writing.  
Repository: https://github.com/adimidla20/oss-audit-24BCG10117

### Game Physics Experiments

Status: experiment archive, not a single released game.  
C# explorations of motion, vectors, collisions, and particle effects.  
Repository: https://github.com/adimidla20/Gamephysics_projects

### VR Parkour Game

Status: learning prototype. No public demo link was supplied.  
The supplied project information describes exploration with Unity and the XR Interaction Toolkit, including climbing and grabbing, physics-led movement, A* pathfinding, and ghost-trail guidance. The site does not claim that every explored mechanic is complete.

### Escape the Quiet Room

Status: VR concept / learning exercise.  
A single-player escape-room idea involving environmental puzzles, teleportation locomotion, and comfort-oriented VR design.

### Float Quest: The Lost Inventor

Status: educational game concept.  
An idea inspired by Archimedes’ principle and buoyancy, using exploration and raft-building as possible interactive learning mechanics.

### Interactive projectile-motion study

A small in-site experiment implemented for this portfolio. Visitors can adjust angle, initial speed, and gravity, and compare the resulting ideal trajectory, range, peak height, and flight time. It is not listed as a prior project. The model omits air resistance.
